newsitem.title: PORTUGAL: Opel, Ford halt output in Portugal.
newsitem.headline: Opel, Ford halt output in Portugal.

text.p: Opel, a unit of U.S. carmaker General Motors Corp, and Ford shut factories in Portugal on Wednesday because of a dire shortage of parts held up by a two-week-old Spanish truck drivers' strike, officials said.
"We have no supplies," said Ford spokesman Artur Lemos.

He told Reuters that some 400 workers were not working on Wednesday at Ford's factory at Azambuja, 30 km (19 miles) north of Lisbon, which assembles Ford Transit vans. The factory normally produces 50 vehicles per day.
Production at the factory was halted on Friday and Monday.
Spokesman Miguel Tome said two shifts totalling 900 workers at Opel's Azambuja factory were not working on Wednesday.
"It is still not possible to predict whether we can work tomorrow," he told Reuters.
The Opel factory, which normally assembles 240 Opel Combo and Opel Corsa vans per day, operated at 40 percent capacity on Tuesday, he said.
